turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Yeah, hi. Ready when you are.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Went to bed proper around one, but I'd already crashed on the couch before that — dozed off with the TV on around midnight, then woke up stiff and dragged myself to bed about three.
Thanks for explaining that. Approximately how many hours do you think you actually slept in total last night? And would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Went to bed proper around one, but I'd already crashed on the couch before that — dozed off with the TV on around midnight, then woke up stiff and dragged myself to bed about three.

Interviewer just said: Thanks for explaining that. Approximately how many hours do you think you actually slept in total last night? And would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Eh, maybe six, six and a half if you count the couch time. Slept fine once I was actually out — just annoyed at myself for waking up stiff on that couch again. Wasn't bad sleep, just poorly organized sleep, if that makes sense.
That does make sense, thank you. What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed, and why did you choose to do that activity?
"Just the TV, honestly. Same as always — leave it low, let it run till I nod off, don't put much thought into it."
Thanks. What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Eh, honestly, nothing special — mostly just the couch thing happening more than usual, dozing off there and waking up stiff instead of going straight to bed. Other than that, same as it's been for a while: no real schedule, up whenever, nap whenever, doesn't seem to hurt me much.
Is that pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep and routine?
Not much has changed — same drill as usual, no real bedtime, nap when I feel like it. The couch thing's been happening a bit more lately, but that's about it.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Not really, no — but I don't lose sleep over it, so to speak. The couch thing's annoying, but the actual sleeping part's fine when it happens. I just wish I'd quit falling asleep out there instead of just going to bed like a normal person.
Thanks for explaining that. You've probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Yeah, not really practical, no — I'm usually up till one or so and my body just does what it wants after that. I don't fight it much. Numbers like that always struck me as more of a guideline for other people than something I need to hit.
What tends to make it easier or harder for you to actually get that much sleep, in your case?

Mostly it's the couch — if I make it to bed at a decent hour instead of crashing out in front of the TV, I get more of it. Working those three mornings helps too, keeps me from sleeping clean through till noon. Other than that, nothing much makes it easier or harder, it just kind of happens or it doesn't.
Many people check their phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this too? Why or why not?
Nah, not really — no phone or tablet in bed with me. TV's usually already on low as background noise, but that's about it.
Thanks, that’s clear. Do you regularly use social media at other times of day? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?
No, not really — I never got into that Facebook and Twitter stuff, my kids keep telling me to sign up but I never bothered. TV's about as much screen as I care for.
Got it, thanks. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
Nah, I don't mess with those. My kids have brought it up, same as the social media stuff, but I never had a reason to try it.
Thanks, that’s helpful to know. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
"Sleeping in the bed instead of the couch, probably. But I've been meaning to fix that for six years now, so I wouldn't hold my breath."
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think switching from the couch to your bed more consistently is actually doable for you? Why or why not?
"Doable, sure — I'm only out those three mornings. Rest of it's just habit at this point, not like anything's stopping me but me."

Thanks for explaining that. Now I have a few quick background questions. (Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.)

What is your age, your profession, your country of birth, your current country of residence, and—if different from your birth country—when did you move?
"58, worked mostly in shipping and receiving before I cut back to part-time — do inventory now at the hardware store a few mornings a week. Born here, lived here my whole life, never moved anywhere."
Thanks for sharing that. Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep, your evening routines, or anything we’ve talked about today that you’d like to add?
